To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the proton-antiprotron scattering data confirm the general predictions of axiomatic field theories, that they also confirm the conventional models, and that they eliminate certain unorthodox possibilities.

the proton-antiprotron elastic scattering cross-section at the ISR energy is 25.7 ± 2.2 mb and the total cross-section is 59 ± 5 mb, and the ratio of the real to the imaginary part of the forward proton-antipropton elastic scattering amplitude at ISR energies is 1.1 ± 0.2.

the proton-antiprotron elastic cross-sections at the ISR are very close to the proton-proton cross-sections, that the total cross-section for proton-antipropton is about 10% higher than the proton-proton total cross-section, and that the ratio of the real parts of the forward scattering amplitudes for pp and pp is very close to unity.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the data from the ISR and SPS are consistent with a conventional description of hadronic collisions in terms of the exchange of a small number of Regge poles and that there is no need to invoke new physics.

the data are consistent with the conventional view that the proton-antiprotron total cross-section is dominated by a single exchange process with the exchange particle having the quantum numbers of a photon and a mass in the range of 1 GeV/c2.
the proton-proton data are not in contradiction with axiomatic field theories and the proton-antiprotons data do not show any deviation from the proton-proton ones.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proton-proton data are not inconsistent with conventional ideas, but they are not conclusive in any direction either.
the present experiments have already confirmed many aspects of our theoretical predictions and that there is no need to introduce any new “unorthodox” ideas.
the proton-antiprotons diffractive scattering is in agreement with the conventional models and that it does not show any sign for the existence of a non-orthodox interaction.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there are many new things to be learned in the future from proton-antiparticle collisions.

the data from proton-antiprton scattering at CERN are in excellent agreement with the predictions of axiomatic field theories, which are based on the principles of unitarity and analyticity and which have no free parameters.
